description:
## Problem
`src/vug/fetcher.cr:115-128` (`apply_action`) is hard to read. The method:
1. Dispatches to `handle_result_action` for state mutation, then
2. Uses early `return` and fall-through logic based on the same action enum.

The two methods (`apply_action` and `handle_result_action`) share knowledge of which actions mutate state vs. which produce a result, leading to dense control flow.

## Fix
Make `apply_action` a pure dispatcher: it returns a `Result?` to terminate the loop, or `nil` to continue. Keep `handle_result_action` purely for state mutation (no value returns). Suggested shape:

```crystal
private def apply_action(action : Action, next_url : String?, result : Result, state : LoopState) : Result?
  case action
  when .redirect?, .try_fallback?
    handle_result_action(action, next_url, state)
    # Redirect always continues; TryFallback with a next_url also continues.
    # TryFallback without a next_url returns the result.
    action.try_fallback? && next_url.nil? ? result : nil
  when .return_result?
    result
  when .use_cached?
    next_url ? Vug.success(state.current_url, next_url) : result
  end
end
```

(Exact shape TBD by implementer — the goal is: one method returns "should I stop the loop?", the other only mutates state.)

## Why
- Readability: clear separation between "mutate state" and "decide to stop".
- Testability: each method has a single responsibility.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `apply_action` is the only method that decides loop termination.
- [ ] `handle_result_action` only mutates `state`.
- [ ] All existing tests in `spec/vug/fetcher_spec.cr` and `spec/vug/fetcher_logic_spec.cr` still pass.
- [ ] Public API unchanged.

## Out of scope
- Do not change the `Action` enum.
- Do not touch the `fetch_loop` body beyond what the refactor requires.
title: fetcher: simplify apply_action control flow
